Wednesday’s decision will also protect hundreds of jobs in Scotland and add almost £3bn to the UK economy over the lifetime of the project. proposals.reasoning: Channel logic (conservative, headline‑only evidence): 1) Larger US deficits financed at higher yields push up global interest rates and risk premia, raising Square Country borrowing costs and interest payments on public and private debt. 2) Tighter financial conditions mildly slow domestic activity, lowering near‑term GDP growth and tax receipts and raising unemployment a little. 3) A stronger USD / higher global rates can weigh on demand for Square exports to the US and raise import financing costs, reducing trade volumes modestly. 4) Effects are first‑stage and small relative to Square Country's large economy; we avoid assuming any US policy changes beyond the reported deficit and higher yields. Numbers are conservative and reflect short‑to‑medium‑term impacts given the evidence level.

sources.title: ‘Pure arrogance’: anger in Finland as Google illegally fells 250,000 trees for datacentre
sources.summary: Company ordered to stop work at two sites in country, which has found itself at forefront of tech firms’ latest push Behind a wire fence lies a vast gaping wound of earth. Before Google’s arrival a few months ago, an estimated quarter of a million trees occupied the 330 hectares (815 acres) of forest near the town of Muhos in rural northern Finland. Now they are all gone. After the tech company illegally stripped the entire area to build a datacentre – taking even the top soil with it – all that remains is a vast expanse of mud indented with the trail marks of machinery, puddles and mounds of earth, roots and branches. Residents say that brown water flowing off the site is going into a stream that feeds the Oulujoki River. Continue reading...
